title: bridge: RQ-PHX-CHANNELREPLYLAG96
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-CHANNELREPLYLAG96` (pool: devin), single commit on base `34ea67b85`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-CHANNELREPLYLAG96 — per-channel reply lag on the Channels pane

## What Mason now sees

Each row of the desktop Channels pane (`src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-channels/`)
gains two lines from the owner thread:

- **Last from Mason** — age and a one-line, 80-char preview of his newest
  inbound message on that channel (e.g. `Last from Mason 15m ago · Phantom status`).
- **Leader reply** — age of the first outbound/Leader message on the same
  channel after it (`Leader reply 5m ago`), or `Leader reply unanswered`.

When a message has been unanswered for more than 10 minutes, the row shows a
red `waiting Nm` chip, and a header line above the rows reads
`N channel(s) waiting on the Leader`. Read-only: nothing was added that can
send.

## Data source

No server change was needed. `GET /api/verse/comms/owner-thread`
(`src/core/verse/owner-thread-api.ts`, schema `comms.owner-thread.v1`) already
returns messages carrying `channel`, `direction` (`inbound`/`outbound`), `at`
and `text`. The pane consumes the existing `ownerThreadQuery` hook
(`leader-thread/owner-thread-queries.ts`) — reusing the same `QueryDef` shares
its cache with the Leader thread and window-title readers instead of double-
fetching the same route. The pane polls it on the same 15 s tick as the
fleet-runs snapshot. Raw channels the board does not list (e.g. `slack`) fold
into the `Other` row through the existing `channelKey()` mapping and are named
in the line (`Slack · Last from Mason …`); `channelName()` from
`owner-thread-lines.ts` supplies the display name.

## Files

- NEW `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-channels/channel-reply-lag.ts` —
  pure `deriveChannelReplyLag(messages, nowMs)` keyed by owner-thread channel
  id, plus `replyLagForRow` (row fold) and `channelsWaiting` (header count).
  "After" is thread order; messages with unparseable `at` are skipped.
- NEW `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-channels/ChannelReplyLag.tsx` — per-row
  component rendering the two lines and the red chip.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-channels/FleetChannelsPane.tsx` — imports,
  the `ownerThreadQuery` read folded into the existing poll, the header count,
  one JSX line per row.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-channels/fleet-channels.module.css` —
  `.waitingChip` (status-danger tokens).
- `FleetChannelsPane.test.tsx` / `FleetChannelsPane.mirror.test.tsx` — poll
  fetch-count expectations updated for the added per-tick owner-thread read
  (1→2 per tick; 3→4 per tick). No assertion weakened.

## Tests

- NEW `channel-reply-lag.test.ts` — answered; unanswered under/over 10 min;
  reply on a different channel does not count; several Mason messages in a row
  (both directions); 80-char preview truncation; bad-clock rows; row fold and
  waiting count.
- NEW `FleetChannelsPane.replylag96.test.tsx` — a Slack row with an
  unanswered "Phantom status" 15 min old shows `waiting 15m` and the header
  count of 1; an answered channel shows the reply age with no chip and no
  header; a missing owner-thread route renders no reply lines.

## Commands run (all with a temporary HOME)

- `npm run install:worktree` — worktree node_modules was missing eslint's
  `lib/`; pnpm 10.28.2 frozen install + heal restored it.
- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-channels/` —
  **15 files / 77 tests, all pass.**
- `npx eslint <all seven changed/new files>` — clean, 0 findings (one run per
  file set, foreground).
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — **exit 0.**
- `git fetch origin master` — HEAD already at `34ea67b85`; `git diff --stat`
  shows 4 tracked files; nothing committed.

## Limitations

- The owner-thread route is dispatch-gated; on builds/sessions without it the
  pane silently shows no reply lines (404 → empty read, by the query's design).
- Reply debt derives from the last 100 thread messages; an unanswered Mason
  message older than that window drops out of view.
- Channels the owner thread does not cover (`page`, `terminal`, `fleet-say`,
  `mobile`) never show a lag — by design, there is nothing to answer there.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-COMMSSTATUSPATH101
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-COMMSSTATUSPATH101` (pool: devin), single commit on base `34ea67b85`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-COMMSSTATUSPATH101

## Summary

Integration qualification of the email-to-Leader status round trip (Mason
t1618u/t1620u/t1627u and the outstanding natural-language "Phantom status"
channel requests). One new test file, `test/comms-status-path-101.test.ts`
(+347 lines), proves a real status answer reaches a durable reply through the
existing intake — no production code was changed; the integration exposed no
defect in `src/core/comms/email-fleet-status.ts`.

The suite drives `runEmailDropOnce` (the exported bridge pass entry,
`src/core/comms/email-drop-bridge.ts:532`) wired exactly the way
`cmdEmailCycle` wires it (`src/cli/comms.ts:360-399`): a real
`email-drop.json` written/read through `writeEmailDropConfig` /
`readEmailDropConfig` names the tmp inbox/outbox/processed folders and the
`from` allowlist. Only the two designed seams are substituted: the local
fleet readers via `EmailDropRecordOptions.statusReaders`
(`email-drop-bridge.ts:93`, typed by `EmailFleetStatusReaders` in
`email-fleet-status.ts:6-10`) and the mail transport via
`sendEmailOutbox`'s `EmailTransport` (`email-outbox.ts:64`). Intake, sender
verification (allowlist + pairing + exact-domain DKIM, `operator-proof.ts`),
the permanent `queue/email-status-seen/<sha256>` claim, response
construction, and the outbox `sending/`→`sent/` claim protocol all run real.

## What the five tests prove

1. `/fleet-status` from a paired, allowlisted, DKIM-passing operator yields
   `status-queued` and exactly one `status-<sha256(messageId)>.reply.eml`
   correlated by `In-Reply-To`/`References`, subject `Re: Phantom fleet
   status`, with the real measured counts (`Runs status`, `running`,
   `target`, `queued`, `held lanes`, `Live workers`, `Leader passes`,
   `Orchestrator agents`, `Supply`, `Planner`). It is not an inbox receipt:
   no `MASON-INBOX.md`, no `Inbox:` preview. The request file moves to
   `processed/`, the claim file persists, `sendEmailOutbox` delivers it via
   the fake transport to `sent/`. A redelivery of the same Message-ID is
   `status-duplicate` — no second reply, readers not re-invoked, transport
   still at one call.
2. A rejecting `runs` reader yields `Runs status: unavailable` while the
   workers and supply lines stay measured; the thrown diagnostic
   (`reader diag /private/reader-root exploded`) never reaches the email.
3. Reader payloads stay counts-only: secret-shaped lane names, held
   reasons, events text, job/repo identifiers and a non-allowlisted supply
   lane (`Supply: none ready`) never leak; the tmp root path and the
   operator's own subject text are absent.
4. The natural-language asks `status` and `fleet status` each earn the
   threaded `Re: Phantom` operator glance (deterministic empty-state text
   `Running unknown.` / `Main health unknown.`), claim dedupe identical,
   status readers never consulted.
5. An unallowlisted sender and an unpaired/DKIM-failing allowlisted sender
   are both silently refused (`refused=2`, no reply, no inbox, no reader
   calls, files still archived to `processed/`). Outbound, a reply
   addressed to a non-allowlisted recipient becomes a pending draft under
   `runsDir/drafts/` and moves to `drafted/` — the transport is never
   invoked for it.

## Commands run and results

- `git fetch origin master` — clean; worktree HEAD 34ea67b859, no drift at finish.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/comms-status-path-101.test.ts`
  — first run: 2 fixture errors in my test (outbox name order is
  content-hash sorted, not name order; outbox dir absent when nothing was
  written). After fixes: **5/5 pass** (~1.9 s), and re-run after the
  node_modules repair below: **5/5 pass** again.
- `npx eslint test/comms-status-path-101.test.ts` — **clean** (initial run
  failed to start: this worktree's `node_modules/eslint` lacked `lib/`;
  repaired with the sanctioned `npm run install:worktree`
  (pnpm 10.28.2 frozen-lockfile, shared same-volume store), after which
  eslint ran clean).
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — **exit 0**, foreground,
  no diagnostics (tsgo 7.0.0-dev.20260707.2 from node_modules).
- `git diff --stat` / `git status --porcelain` — only
  `?? test/comms-status-path-101.test.ts` and this file; nothing committed.

## Net LOC

+347 test, 0 production. `src/core/comms/email-fleet-status.ts` untouched —
the integration surfaced no defect there.

## Limitations

- The ask path (`status`/`fleet status` bodies) exercises
  `readOperatorGlance` against an empty tmp runs dir, so only its
  deterministic empty-state lines are asserted, not populated counts.
- The send leg asserts transport arguments and the `sent/` move through an
  injected fake `EmailTransport`; Mail.app/osascript is never invoked (per
  the no-live-transport constraint).
- `runPass` mirrors `cmdEmailCycle`'s wiring rather than calling
  `cmdComms(['email-cycle'])` itself, because the CLI path offers no
  `statusReaders` seam — deterministic counts require the injected readers.
</details>

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-REDTYPEFIXSIXTH88` (pool: devin), single commit on base `085b292a6`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-REDTYPEFIXSIXTH88 — land a real Quick-typecheck failure

## Source PR

**#4698 — `bridge: RQ-PHX-IDEASDRAFTUIRECOVER10SRS2`** (head `480adf9490`, merge-base `3bba3902`, base noted by author `e6182c6b6`).
Carries the Ideas "Draft job" UI recovery for the still-open original PR #4348:
selection of 2–8 ideas, single and batch draft posts to `POST /api/ideas/draft`,
collision confirmation, an in-flight duplicate guard and a result chip, plus two
test files. All carried work is inside `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/`.

Closes #4698.

## Candidate enumeration (why this PR)

Method: listed the 100 newest open PRs, mapped each head branch to its latest CI
run, and kept PRs whose only failing jobs were `Quick typecheck` (+ the cascading
`Merge Gate`). Held PRs (#1487, #1488, #2444), release-train PRs and PRs with an
existing fix/recut naming them were excluded. Actions job logs need admin rights
for this repo (`403 Must have admin rights` unauthenticated), so "real TS error"
was confirmed exactly the way CI does it: the Quick typecheck job checks out the
PR head sha and runs `npm run typecheck` = `tsgo --noEmit` + `tsgo --noEmit -p
src/web-ui/tsconfig.json`. Each candidate's full head tree was extracted and both
tsgo projects were run (`@typescript/native-preview@7.0.0-dev.20260707.2`).

Newest-first results across 47 candidates (#4754–#4633; #4754/#4742/#4701 had no
CI runs at all; every other PR's Quick typecheck run was red):

| PR | head-tree tsgo result |
|----|-----------------------|
| 4750, 4749, 4744, 4734, 4725, 4723, 4722 | 0 errors (failures are bind/authority-drift/generated-file steps, not TS) |
| 4717, 4715, 4706, 4702 | 0 errors |
| **4719** | **1 real error: TS2352, `src/web-ui/routes/verse/resources/first-read.test.ts(52,52)`** |
| **4698** | **2 real errors: TS2322 ×2, `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas-original-4348-roundtrip-10srs2.test.tsx(16,30)`** |
| 4697, 4696, 4692, 4685, 4683, 4681, 4678, 4675, 4674, 4673, 4672, 4671, 4670 | 0 errors |
| 4669, 4667, 4665, 4664, 4663, 4661, 4660, 4653, 4652, 4651, 4650, 4649, 4647, 4646, 4644, 4641, 4639, 4638, 4636, 4634, 4633 | 0 errors |

Exactly **2** confirmed real-TS-error candidates exist — fewer than six — so per
the job spec the **last** one was taken: **#4698**. (#4719's TS2352 conversion of
an unrelated fixture shape remains for a future pass.)

## The error and the fix

Reported errors (reproduced verbatim on the PR head tree):

```
src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas-original-4348-roundtrip-10srs2.test.tsx(16,70): error TS2322:
  Type '() => Promise<Response>' is not assignable to type '(url: string, body: Record<string, unknown>) => Response | undefined'.
src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas-original-4348-roundtrip-10srs2.test.tsx(30,70): error TS2322:
  Type '() => Promise<never> | Response' is not assignable to type '(url: string, body: Record<string, unknown>) => Response | undefined'.
```

The PR's new roundtrip test hands `stubSurfaceFetch` a `post` handler that returns
a promise (a held pending response in one test, a rejected `TypeError` retry in
the other). The stub already runs `post` inside an `async` fetch mock and returns
its result, so a `Promise<Response>` works at runtime; only the declared
signature in `StubOptions` was too narrow.

Fix (the "correct a signature" case): widened the member to
`post?: (url: string, body: Record<string, unknown>) => Response | Promise<Response> | undefined`
in `src/web-ui/routes/verse/command/fetch-stub.test-support.ts` (test-support
file, one line, no `any`/casts/`ts-ignore`, no tsconfig change). Sync handlers in
all existing suites remain assignable; `options.post?.(u,b) ?? json({ok:true})`
in the async mock unwraps the promise unchanged.

## Files

Source PR changed **6** paths; carried diff is **7** paths (+1 signature-fix
file, `fetch-stub.test-support.ts`; no alternative inside the PR's own files can
give a promise-returning handler a synchronous `Response` type without a cast or
weakening the test). Plus this note file.

- A `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/IdeaDraftChip.tsx` (+44)
- A `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/IdeasPane.draft.test.tsx` (+64)
- M `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/IdeasPane.tsx` (+44/−4)
- M `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas-model.ts` (+2)
- A `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas-original-4348-roundtrip-10srs2.test.tsx` (+49)
- M `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas.module.css` (+5)
- M `src/web-ui/routes/verse/command/fetch-stub.test-support.ts` (+1/−1, the fix)

No `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS-listed paths, `src/cli/fleet.ts`, `package.json`
`files`, docs index pages, desktop or release config touched. No secrets.

## Commands run and results

- `git archive`/`git fetch origin pull/<N>/head` per candidate; head trees
  extracted under `/tmp` (worktree stayed clean until the carry).
- Per candidate: `tsgo --noEmit` + `tsgo --noEmit -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json`
  (`@typescript/native-preview@7.0.0-dev.20260707.2`, the version pinned in
  devDependencies). Baseline `origin/master` (`42a385c578`): both exit 0.
- Carried change: `tsgo --noEmit` → exit 0; `tsgo --noEmit -p
  src/web-ui/tsconfig.json` → exit 0 (the two TS2322s gone, no new errors).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx --no-install vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/IdeasPane.draft.test.tsx
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/ideas-original-4348-roundtrip-10srs2.test.tsx`
  → 2 files, **6 tests passed / 0 failed** (pending-promise and rejection
  behavior exercised through the widened signature).
- Neighboring `post`-helper suites `CommandSection.test.tsx` +
  `LeaderThreadPane.held.test.tsx` → **30 tests passed / 0 failed** (no
  regression from the widened signature).
- `node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js` on all 7 changed TS/TSX files →
  clean, 0 findings. (The repo's eslint package shipped a missing `lib/`;
  restored `lib/` from the same-version `eslint@9.39.5` tarball before running —
  same gap the source PR's own notes hit.)
- Final sanctioned check: `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`
  (tsgo restored into node_modules from the npx cache, version
  7.0.0-dev.20260707.2) — result recorded below.

Nothing committed, pushed or tagged; all changes are uncommitted in the worktree.
</details>

  fallback, `--json` shape, verdict-first human output. All fixtures are

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-HANDOFFSPOOLTTL10SSC2
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-HANDOFFSPOOLTTL10SSC2` (pool: devin), single commit on base `cc0dc6f58`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-HANDOFFSPOOLTTL10SSC2

## Summary

`runContextReplyDelivery` stamped a failed reply publication with
`preparedAt: Date.now()` at spool-save time. Two defects followed:

1. **Clock incoherence** — the retry/drain path ages records on
   `(bus.now ?? Date.now)()`, so an injected bus clock made the wall-clock
   stamp read as rollback (or worse, granted life on a skewed domain).
2. **Late stamp** — `runContextReply` prepares the reply envelope, then
   attempts `publishContextReply` *inside* the producer before returning.
   Stamping after the failed attempt let a slow publication (or any
   post-preparation delay) push the retained deadline later than the reply
   it retains, extending the effective TTL by that gap.

The producer (`context-result-bus.ts`, read-only) does not expose its
preparation instant, so the fix derives a conservative bound inside the
spool module from existing timing contracts:

- `runContextReply` computes `reply.ttl = request.ttl - ceil(perfElapsed)`,
  so `request.ttl - reply.ttl` is exactly the consumed budget. Re-anchoring
  that budget on a bus-clock reading taken *before* the run lands at (or
  just before, minus a 2 ms skew covering the producer's `ceil()` and
  capture jitter) the true preparation instant — the retained deadline
  becomes ≈ delivery start + original request TTL, immune to publication
  duration.
- The request file is read before and after the run; identical canonical
  bytes plus `body.inReplyTo === request.id` are required for the derived
  stamp. Otherwise the stamp falls back to the earliest observed bus-clock
  reading (or 0), which can only shorten — never extend — remaining life.
- Invalid/throwing/negative bus clocks yield no stamp and fall back the
  same way; `savePendingContextReply`'s existing validation is unchanged.

Retry semantics are untouched: `deliverSpooledContextReply` still measures
`elapsed = now - preparedAt` on the bus clock, refuses `clock-rollback` and
`expired`, republishes through `publishContextReply` (backdated admission,
exact wire bytes, bus dedupe), and never reruns the worker.

## Files

- `src/core/fleet/context-reply-spool.ts` (+64/-1): `busClockStamp`,
  `requestStampSource`, `spooledPreparedAt` helpers; `runContextReplyDelivery`
  captures bus-clock marks and request snapshots around `runContextReply`.
- `test/handoff-spool-age-preservation-10ssc2.test.ts` (new, 174 lines):
  real delivery path (`cmdFleetContextDeliver` → `runContextReplyDelivery`)
  with a synthetic `node -e` worker, temp bus/spool dirs, held
  `bus-inbox/writer.lock` for a real publication failure, and a fully
  synthetic injected bus clock (`T0 = 1_000_000`, far from `Date.now`).

## Test coverage vs acceptance

- **Slow failed publication + advance beyond lifetime → expired**: the
  worker's last stderr byte advances the injected clock by 20 s inside the
  publication window; drain at `T0 + ttl + delay` reports `expired: 1`,
  retains the record byte-identical, posts nothing, marker shows one spawn.
  Also asserts `preparedAt === T0 + (request.ttl - reply.ttl) - 2` exactly.
- **Retry inside remaining lifetime posts once**: drain at
  `preparedAt + 1000` posts; `receivedAt === preparedAt` proves backdated
  admission; envelope wire fields unchanged; second drain selects 0.
- **Successive drains dedupe**: covered above (record removed on post).
- **Clock rollback refuses**: drain at `preparedAt - 1` → `clock-rollback`,
  record retained.
- **Injected bus clock coherence**: the synthetic clock makes any
  `Date.now()` stamp a rollback; all stamps now use `bus.now ?? Date.now`.
- **Unusable bus clock**: throwing `now` → `preparedAt: 0` fallback,
  worker outcome still reported, drain reports `expired`, no rerun.
- No real TTL sleeps anywhere.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/handoff-spool-age-preservation-10ssc2.test.ts`
  → 4/4 passed (~4 s).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/context-reply-spool.integration.test.ts
  test/handoff-reply-retry-proof88.test.ts test/handoff-bus-reply-roundtrip.test.ts`
  → 24/25 passed; the one failure is **pre-existing on clean HEAD**
  (verified via `git stash`): `handoff-reply-retry-proof88` expects
  `body.taskId` in the reply wire, which `runContextReply` does not emit —
  unrelated to this change (producer files are read-only here).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-context-drain.test.ts
  test/context-drain-continuation.test.ts test/fleet-context-watch-recovery.test.ts
  test/handoff-receive-deadline-10ssb1.test.ts test/handoff-worker-cancel-10ssb2.test.ts`
  → 86/86 passed.
- `npx eslint src/core/fleet/context-reply-spool.ts
  test/handoff-spool-age-preservation-10ssc2.test.ts` → clean (0 errors,
  0 warnings; caught and fixed a missing `.test(name)` in the test filter).
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → exit 0, no output.
- `npm run install:worktree` was run once to repair a partial
  `node_modules/eslint` install (missing `lib/`); node_modules only, no
  tracked files touched.
- `git fetch origin master` before finishing; `git diff FETCH_HEAD` shows no
  upstream drift in `context-reply-spool.ts`, `context-result-bus.ts`,
  `bus-inbox.ts`, or `context-spool-drain.ts` since the worktree base.

## Net LOC

`src/core/fleet/context-reply-spool.ts` +64/-1; new test +174; BRIDGE_NOTES.md
+~95. Well under the ~400 changed-line budget for code+test.

## Remaining limits

- The derived stamp trusts that the request file's canonical bytes are
  stable across the run; a concurrent rewrite-and-revert between the two
  bracket reads is not detectable in-module (producer is read-only). The
  `inReplyTo` cross-check and the earlier-is-safer fallback bound the
  residual risk; the file is operator-private input.
- Arbitrary mid-run clock jumps on an injected `bus.now` are bounded by the
  existing retry-side `clock-rollback` refusal; the stamp uses the earliest
  coherent observation.
- `deliverSpooledContextReply` still reads `now` once for `elapsed` and
  `publishContextReply` re-reads it for admission (`receivedAt = at -
  elapsed`); the sub-millisecond skew between the two reads is unchanged
  pre-existing behavior in a read-only-adjacent path.
- Pre-existing failure noted above (`handoff-reply-retry-proof88` taskId
  expectation) is out of scope; flagged for the owning lane.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-STEERTARGETOUTCOME90
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-STEERTARGETOUTCOME90` (pool: devin), single commit on base `cc0dc6f58`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-STEERTARGETOUTCOME90 — steer-target outcome lines in the Leader thread

Serves Mason t1627u (working two-way Leader thread in the desktop app) and
t1628u (Phantom must answer him in the app). Closes the loop opened by
RQ-PHX-STEERJOBTARGET87 (#4751): when a Mason entry aims a steer order at one
job (`@RQ-id`), the Leader thread now shows one follow-up line under that
entry once the job has an outcome.

## What changed (4 files)

- **New `src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/steer-target-outcome.ts`** —
  pure model. `steerTargetId(entryText)` reuses `targetsOf` from
  `fleet/interject-target-model.ts` (the parser #4751 added; no second parser
  written). `steerTargetOutcome(entryText, jobFacts)` returns
  `{ id, stage, text, href? } | null`: `null` when the entry names no target;
  `still running (since <time>)` when the job detail says running or the live
  workers list holds it; `merged as #N` (+ link) on trace/merges evidence;
  `finished, PR #N open` (+ link) on publish evidence; `ended empty` when the
  publish file exists with no PR; `failed: no publish result` when the run was
  reaped without writing a result; `RQ-X: no outcome recorded yet` otherwise.
  Unknown stays unknown — no guessing. PR links are validated as
  `https://github.com/.../pull/<n>`; off-site or credentialed urls never link.

- **Edited `src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/LeaderThreadPane.tsx`** —
  new `SteerTargetLine` component renders the follow-up (quiet `system`-styled
  line, `data-steer-outcome` stage attribute) under each Mason line whose text
  names a target. Job facts reuse existing reads only — **no new server
  route**: `ordersTraceQuery` (`/api/verse/leader/orders`, the read the Inbox
  outcome chips share), `readMerges(runs.data)` and `narrowWorkers(runs.data)`
  on the fleet-runs read the pane already polls, and `jobDetailQuery(id)`
  (`/api/fleet/job?id=`, the JobDetailSheet query) polled at 10 s while the
  pane is visible.

- **New `steer-target-outcome.test.ts`** — covers merged (trace and
  merges-window evidence), merged without a number, non-GitHub url never
  linked, open PR (detail + pending evidence), ended empty, failed, running
  (detail and live-worker paths, live beats stale history), unknown/queued/
  launched-only, and entries with no `@RQ-id` returning `null`.

- **New `LeaderThreadPane.steer-target.test.tsx`** — renders the pane with a
  targeted Mason inbox entry + a merged job fact; asserts the
  `RQ-PHX-FIX merged as #4321` line links to the PR; covers the
  no-outcome-recorded and no-target cases.

## Design notes

- One line per entry, first `@RQ-id` wins (matches the single-target steer
  box). Order: live run > merged > open PR > ended > unknown — a live run is
  current truth; a recorded RESULT with no PR reads as `ended empty`; a reaped
  run with no RESULT reads as `failed: no publish result`.
- `fleet.job.v1` does not project the RESULT class (EMPTY vs ABORT/DENIED), so
  "ended empty" is the closest honest label for published-without-PR, and
  `archived` (log.gz, no publish) is the only unambiguous failure evidence —
  reported as `failed: no publish result`, a fact, not a guess.
- The order trace only knows jobs whose prompts cite an order key; jobs it
  misses fall through to detail/merges/workers evidence, then "no outcome
  recorded yet".

## Commands run and results

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/steer-target-outcome.test.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/LeaderThreadPane.steer-target.test.tsx`
  → **18/18 pass**.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/` → **148/148 pass, 33 files** (all
  existing LeaderThreadPane suites still green).
- `npx eslint <4 changed files>` → clean. (Worktree's eslint package was
  missing `lib/`; repaired by symlinking `lib` from the pnpm store — a
  node_modules fix only, nothing tracked.)
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → **tsgo absent in this
  worktree** (`@typescript/native-preview` not linked; npx 404). Fallback per
  job rules: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → **exit 0**, and
  `npx tsc --noEmit -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json` (the project covering the
  changed files) → **exit 0**.
- `git fetch origin master` → HEAD is `f21bdc4d8` = origin/master; work is
  uncommitted on top of it.

## Diff

`git diff --stat` shows 4 files (LeaderThreadPane.tsx +56/−5, plus 3 new
files) — inside the 5-file limit. No commits made.
</details>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-STEERSCREENSHOT90

## Mason order served

Mason t1628u: he steers the fleet from screenshots of the installed app, but the
desktop "Tell the leaders" box took text only. Now he can paste or drop a
screenshot onto the box and the next Leader pass gets the file path.

## What changed (6 files)

- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet/interject-image.ts` (new): client helpers —
  PNG/JPEG allow-list, 5 MiB cap, FileReader → base64, chip label.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet/InterjectBox.tsx`: `onPaste` on the textarea
  and `onDrop`/`onDragOver` on the form attach one screenshot; a removable
  `screenshot attached (NN KB) ×` chip (Button `subtle/sm`) shows it; send
  passes the base64 to `postInterjection`; Escape and successful send clear it.
  Attaching or removing the image nulls the request key, so a changed
  attachment mints a fresh requestId and can't be collapsed into a prior send.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet/interject-queries.ts`: `post()`/
  `postInterjection()` take an optional third `image` arg; it's added to the
  wire body as `image` (base64) alongside `text`/`source`/`requestId`.
- `src/core/verse/fleet-runs-api.ts` (`POST /api/verse/fleet/runs/inbox`):
  - `readBody` cap raised for this route to 7 MiB (`INTERJECT_POST_MAX_BODY_BYTES`)
    to fit ~6.7 MiB base64 + 6 KB text.
  - `image` added to the body key whitelist — `path`/`name`/`filename` or any
    other key still 400s, so no client-supplied path can reach disk.
  - `parseInterjectImage`: strict base64, ≤5 MiB decoded, and the PNG or JPEG
    magic bytes decide `ext` — the declared client type is never read.
  - `storeInterjectImage`: writes to
    `<runsDir>/leader/inbound/screens/<UTC yyyymmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha256[:8]>.<ext>`
    via `writePrivateFileAtomically` (dir `mkdirSync` mode 0700, file 0600),
    using the same `deps.runsDir ?? defaultRunsDir()` resolver the route uses.
  - The write runs inside the channel receiver's `write` callback via the
    request ticket, so the ` [image: <abs path>]` tag joins only on an accepted
    append — dedupe keys on text/requestId alone, and the requestId ledger
    replay + receipt store (RQ-PHX-STEERDOUBLESEND83) write no second file.
    A storage failure fails closed as `write-failed` → 503, never a partial line.
- `test/interject-image-route.test.ts` (new) and
  `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet/InterjectBox.image.test.tsx` (new): below.

The route is `src/core/verse/fleet-runs-api.ts` — not under `src/core/desktop/**`.

- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet/InterjectBox.image.test.tsx` — 5/5 pass

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/leader-interject-roundtrip.test.ts
  test/fleet-runs-inbox-durable-dedupe-nov1.test.ts
  test/fleet-runs-inbox-ack-03.test.ts` — 7/7 pass (dedupe intact).

Note: `npm run install:worktree` was needed once — the worktree's eslint
package shipped without `lib/`; the pnpm heal restored it (8378 ms).

Worktree fast-forwarded onto origin/master `f21bdc4d8` (one new commit,

Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-COMPOSERHOLDSTATUS89` (pool: devin), single commit on base `e19af3732`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-COMPOSERHOLDSTATUS89

Desktop Leader composer `/hold <lane> <minutes>` (timed lane hold) and `/status`
(live status line), matching what Telegram already does with `/hold`.

## What changed

- `src/core/fleet/runs-lane-hold.ts` — `parseLaneHoldAction` now returns a
  `LaneHoldAction` union: the existing `{lane, action:'release', reason?}` plus
  `{lane, action:'hold', minutes, reason}`. `minutes` must be an integer
  1..1440; `reason` is printable ASCII ≤120 chars, trimmed, default
  `'held from desktop'`. `minutes` on a release body is rejected.
- `src/core/verse/fleet-holds-api.ts` — POST `{action:'hold'}` dispatches to
  `placeLaneHold` (the same core writer Telegram `/hold` uses — no second hold
  writer) with `changedBy: 'Phantom desktop'`, same mutation-token gate and
  one-action-in-flight guard as release. On the hold verb an `unknown-lane`
  `LaneHoldError` maps to 400; release keeps its 422 contract. Response is the
  refreshed `LaneTargetsV1`. The `placeLaneHold` import is hoisted with the
  other dynamic imports so the in-flight check→assign stays synchronous
  (an `await` in between would have widened the race window).
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-lanes/lane-hold-release.ts` — new
  `postLaneHold(lane, minutes, reason?)` next to `postReleaseHold`, same
  token/`touchMutationHold`/404 handling ("This Phantom server cannot hold
  lanes yet; update the app.").
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/composer-commands.ts` — `hold` and
  `status` specs in `COMPOSER_COMMANDS` (hints/help update automatically), a
  shared `LANE_ARG_RE` for `/release` and `/hold`, exported `holdArgs` splitter,
  and `/hold` arg errors (usage, lane shape, minutes 1–1440).
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/composer-command-run.ts` — new
  `holdLane` and `statusNow` deps (live: `postLaneHold`,
  `fetchLeaderStatusNow`). `/hold` is gated on the mutation token with no
  confirm (safe direction, like release), runs with reason
  `'held from Leader composer'`, confirms `row.held` on the returned targets,
  prints `Held <lane> for <m> min`, posts `[composer] /hold …: done`.
  `/status` is read only (no token, no note): status text, or
  `Status is unavailable right now.`, or `/status failed: <reason>`.
- `docs/api/fleet-openapi.json` — POST holds body is now the release|hold
  `oneOf`; summary updated.
- Tests — new `test/fleet-holds-api-hold.test.ts` (14 tests: hold success +
  targets, reason default/120-char edge, minutes 0/1441/1.5/string/negative/
  missing → 400, bad lane/extra keys/unprintable reason → 400, dispatch + token
  required, unknown lane → 400, manual hold → 422 manual-hold, 200/409
  concurrency, phantom-hold refresh, autobackoff release). New
  `src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread/composer-hold-status.test.ts`
  (4 tests: parse/arg errors, gate shape, /hold success + note, unconfirmed
  hold, /status text|null|throw read-only). Existing composer test files got
  the minimal additions the new commands require (hint list, new dep mocks) —
  no assertions weakened.

## Commands run

- `npm run install:worktree` — healed the worktree's partial deps (eslint's
  `lib/` was missing; without this `npx eslint` cannot start).
- `npx eslint <all 9 changed/new files>` — clean, 0 problems.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-holds-api-hold.test.ts` —
  14/14 pass (after fixing a seconds-precision bound and hoisting the import).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-holds-api.test.ts
  test/fleet-holds-api-hold.test.ts test/runs-lane-hold-31.test.ts
  test/fleet-lane-hold.test.ts test/fleet-openapi-coverage.test.ts` —
  45/46 pass; the one failure is PRE-EXISTING on master:
  `fleet-openapi.json` covers no `/api/verse/fleet/cos/{ask,list,status}`
  paths while `remote-gateway-policy.ts` admits them (verified: 0 cos refs in
  master's spec file, 8 in master's policy source; unrelated to this diff).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/routes/verse/leader-thread` — 31 files, 130/130 pass.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — exit 0.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p src/web-ui/tsconfig.json` — exit 0.

## State

- Nothing committed; 8 modified files + 2 new test files, ~283 net LOC
  (+299 / −16 including new tests).
- `git fetch origin master` just before finishing: master advanced to
  `8b91b707` (bridge RQ-FIX-PHANTOM-3237); it touched only unrelated test
  files — this diff still applies cleanly, no overlap.
</details>

Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-HANDOFFRECEIVEDEADLINE10SSB1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `e19af3732`.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-HANDOFFRECEIVEDEADLINE10SSB1

## Summary

`ashlr fleet handoff-receive` now exposes the bounded worker deadline that
`runContextWorker` already implements, matching the existing `handoff-reply`
wrapper. `HandoffBusReceiveOptions.timeoutMs` is optional and validated (safe
integer 1..3600000) in the same pre-staging refusal block as the other inputs —
before any inbox read, temp staging, or spawn — then forwarded unchanged. The
CLI accepts `--timeout-ms <1..3600000>` (strict `^\d+$` plus integer bounds,
single-occurrence), and this command's usage/example/help text documents it.
No default changed: omitted deadline keeps the worker unbounded, argv after
`--` stays literal, recipient matching, snapshot/task binding, untrusted prompt
wrapping, cwd handling, and temporary-file cleanup are untouched.

## Files changed

- `src/core/fleet/handoff-bus-receive.ts` (+7/-1): optional `timeoutMs` field,
  bounds check in the first invalid-input refusal, forwarded to
  `runContextWorker`.
- `src/cli/fleet-handoff-receive.ts` (+19/-8 net): `--timeout-ms` flag in
  usage, allowed-key list, strict finite-integer validation, forwarded;
  example and help text updated (this command only).
- `test/handoff-receive-deadline-10ssb1.test.ts` (new, ~130 lines):
  - real temporary local inbox envelope + matching snapshot through
    `cmdFleetHandoffReceive`; a Node child that would stay alive is

    duplicate and valueless flags, and invalid API `timeoutMs` all exit 2
    before the inbox reader (`now` uncalled) or spawn;
  - omitted deadline preserves a successful worker and literal argv

  - a quick worker under a large deadline still propagates its exit code.

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-RELEASEEVIDENCEJOIN88
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-RELEASEEVIDENCEJOIN88` (pool: devin), single commit on base `085b292a6`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-RELEASEEVIDENCEJOIN88

## Summary

`readReleaseChainStatus` (`src/core/fleet/release-chain-status.ts`) no longer
attaches the newest `release-sign/v*.log`'s version/reason to the newest
`autorun/sha-<sha>.rc` by recency alone, and rc=0 no longer implies
`published`. The reader now joins evidence to the selected sha only through
existing durable records written by `contrib/mac/release-autorun.sh` (rev2):

- `release-sign/autorun/feed-<sha>.rc` — final published-state outcome
  (0 verified-live, 21 verified-but-superseded, 22 failed).
- `release-sign/autorun/feed-<sha>.json` — receipt, accepted only when it
  parses, `kind === "desktop-update-channel-check"` and `sha` equals the
  selected sha; supplies `state`, `tag` (→ version) and failure `reason`.
- `release-sign/v<semver>-<epoch>.log` — bound only when the log's own
  bounded head carries a `START v<semver> <hexsha>` declaration whose sha
  prefix-matches the selected sha AND whose declared version equals the
  version in the file name. Newest matching log wins; unproven logs are
  never read for reason/version.

Verdict mapping (union unchanged): rc missing/unreadable → `unknown`;
rc=12 → `held`; other non-zero → `failed`; rc=0 → `published` only when
`feed-<sha>.rc` is 0 or 21, `failed` on 22, else `unknown` (signed, publication
unproven). `version`/`reason` are null unless a join above proves them;
new additive `evidence` field reports `versionJoin`, `feedRc`, `feedState`,
`boundLog` and human-readable `diagnostics`. `installedVersion` untouched.
No CLI formatter change was required — it already renders null version as

## What Mason sees

On the desktop live fleet view (Verse → Fleet → Runs graph), a running job

node: "Overrun 2.4x". Hovering the chip shows "Lane median N min"; the node

`schema/fleet-runs.v1.schema.json`). `ratio` is elapsed ÷ lane median rounded
to 3 decimals; `medianMs` is the lane median it was flagged against. Absent

median for that lane. Everything else on the wire is unchanged: same fields,
same ordering; existing `runs`/`workers` source health semantics untouched.

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-INTENTMERGEDTRANSACTION10SSA1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-INTENTMERGEDTRANSACTION10SSA1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `8466a4c6b`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-INTENTMERGEDTRANSACTION10SSA1

## Summary

`ashlr fleet intent-evidence merged --apply` previously did an unlocked
`readLedger -> linkMergedPull -> writeLedger`, so a concurrent
`addIntent`/`updateIntent` (or another evidence writer) committing between the
read and the write was silently dropped — losing another agent's recorded
merge evidence or directive. The apply path now runs `linkMergedPull` inside
`transactIntentLedger`, matching against the freshest locked ledger, the same
primitive `edit.ts`/`import.ts`/`fleet-intent link` already use. Shipped
handling stays delegated to `noteShippedRelease`; dry-run preview, argument
validation, JSON shape and error codes are unchanged. No new lock and no
nested transactions.

No-match behavior: `transactIntentLedger` always persists after `mutate`, so a
`merged --apply` that matches nothing now rewrites the ledger where the old
code skipped the write. For a canonical ledger the rewrite is byte-identical
(proven below); for a non-canonical file it normalizes formatting. A missing
ledger is still never created: `ledgerFilePresent()` gates the transaction and
the legacy read path handles the absent case with zero matches and no write.

## Files changed

- `src/cli/fleet-intent-evidence.ts` (+9/-4 net): import `ledgerFilePresent` +
  `transactIntentLedger` (drop `writeLedger`); merged+apply goes through the
  transaction when the ledger file exists.
- `test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts` (new, ~330 lines): 6 tests.

Net LOC: ~+335/-4 across the two allowed files. BRIDGE_NOTES.md is the only
other changed path.

## Regression evidence

New suite `test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts` drives the real
`cmdFleetIntentEvidence` against an isolated `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR`:

- Child processes (tsx evals) released on a shared go-file barrier race
  `merged --apply` against `addIntent` + `updateIntent`: all three succeed and
  the final ledger keeps the merge evidence (status `merged`, PR association,
  evidence row) AND the concurrent add/update — the exact interleaving the old
  unlocked path could drop.
- Same-process `Promise.all` race through the in-process queue + file lock.
- Held `ledger.lock` (real `acquireLocalStoreLockWithOutcome`): `merged --apply`
  returns exit 1 with `intent-evidence: Intent ledger is busy...` (retryable),
  bytes unchanged; dry-run still answers while locked; retry after release
  applies cleanly.
- Dry-run and unmatched `--apply` leave ledger bytes byte-identical; matched
  apply persists; repeated apply replays safely (one PR association, evidence
  rows accumulate, terminal statuses kept); missing ledger is never created.

Note: the concurrent update uses an `owner` patch, not `evidence` —
`updateIntent` evidence flips `merged`->`verified`, which would make the
post-race status order-dependent. Owner edits never interact with merge status.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts`
  — 6/6 pass (~3.7s).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/intent-evidence-cli-09spc2.test.ts
  test/intent-evidence-reconcile-09spa1.test.ts
  test/intent-release-replay-preservation-09sqv1.test.ts
  test/intent-release-persistence-09spr1.test.ts
  test/intent-link-concurrent-preservation-10sry2.test.ts
  test/intent-sweep-concurrent-preservation-10sry1.test.ts
  test/intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1.test.ts` — 42/42 pass.
- `npx eslint src/cli/fleet-intent-evidence.ts
  test/intent-merged-cli-transaction-10ssa1.test.ts` — clean.
  (This worktree's `node_modules/eslint` was missing `lib/`; restored by copying
  the identical eslint@9.39.5 `lib/` from a sibling worktree — node_modules is
  untracked, no package files touched.)
- `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (via sibling worktree's
  `@typescript/native-preview` binary; this worktree lacks the package) —
  clean, exit 0. Equivalent to `npx --no-install tsgo`; `tsgo` is not published
  on npm under that name.

Pass/fail: all green. No commits, pushes or PRs; changes left uncommitted.

## Remaining limits

- `merged --apply` on an existing but non-canonical ledger file rewrites it in
  canonical `writeLedger` form even when nothing matches (disclosed above);
  bytes are identical for ledgers previously written by `writeLedger`.
- If the ledger file is deleted between `ledgerFilePresent()` and the
  transaction, the transaction creates a fresh empty ledger — same exposure
  any serialized writer has; no code path deletes the ledger in normal use.
- `noteShippedRelease` (release.ts) and merge-snapshot serialization are owned
  by other jobs and were not touched; `shipped --apply` keeps its existing
  semantics.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-INTENTSWEEPSERIAL10SRY1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-INTENTSWEEPSERIAL10SRY1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `2e2a8b918`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-INTENTSWEEPSERIAL10SRY1

## Summary

`sweepStale({ apply: true })` used to `readLedger` → mutate a snapshot →
`writeLedger` with no lock held, so a concurrent `addIntent`/`updateIntent`
committed between its read and write was silently dropped. The apply path now
runs its whole read-compute-mutate-write inside `transactIntentLedger` (the
same primitive `edit.ts`/`import.ts` already use: per-ledger file lock +
in-process queue). The preview path stays a plain unlocked read.

Changed files (uncommitted, exactly as scoped):

- `src/core/intent/sweep.ts` (+23/−10): apply moved into
  `transactIntentLedger`; stale filter factored to `overdue()`. An unlocked
  pre-check read skips the transaction only when nothing is stale, preserving
  the old "no write on no-op apply" behavior (no ledger file is created, no
  bytes rewritten, no lock churn on periodic sweeps). Timestamp validation
  still runs before any store access.
- `test/intent-sweep-concurrent-preservation-10sry1.test.ts` (new, 376 lines):
  9 tests against the real disk store. Deterministic synchronization: a
  one-shot gate on the store's *exported* `readLedger` (vi.mock) holds the
  sweep's unlocked read while real writers commit — on the old code that is
  the apply's only read (deterministic lost write); on the new code it is the
  pre-check read, and the locked read inside `transactIntentLedger` goes
  through a module-internal binding so it never trips the gate. Plus a
  held-lock test and a cross-process go-file barrier test (same pattern as
  `intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1`).

Semantics preserved: stale thresholds, `actionFor`, terminal set, evidence
shape/cap (`MAX_EVIDENCE` slice, fixed note text), `lastTouchedAt`/`updatedAt`
assignments, `{stale, applied, updated}` contract (rows report persisted
post-apply status; `applied` mirrors `opts.apply === true`; `updated` counts
the items the locked transaction actually mutated). No dispatch and no
closure — sweep still only refreshes local tracking.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  test/intent-sweep-concurrent-preservation-10sry1.test.ts`
  → 9/9 pass (new implementation).
- Regression demonstration on the old unlocked implementation
  (`git show HEAD:src/core/intent/sweep.ts` swapped in, same command):
  → 4/9 fail, including both deterministic ones:
  - held-lock test: old apply resolved `{applied:true, updated:1}` under a
    held ledger lock instead of rejecting (wrote inside another writer's
    transaction window);
  - gated interleave test: persisted swept record evidence was
    `[note, sweep]` — the `concurrent verification` row committed mid-sweep
    was silently dropped (the lost-write bug);
  - child-barrier and in-process tests also failed (both concurrent sweeps
    reported `updated:1`; a clobbered apply left the record `in-progress`).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism`
  on the sibling suites
  `test/intent-sweep-applied-result-09spv1.test.ts`
  `test/intent-sweep-preservation-09sqr1.test.ts`
  `test/intent-ledger-module-compat-09sqe1.test.ts`
  `test/intent-preservation-export-audit-09sqm2.test.ts` → 7/7 pass;
  `test/intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1.test.ts` → 6/6 pass.
- `npx eslint src/core/intent/sweep.ts
  test/intent-sweep-concurrent-preservation-10sry1.test.ts` → clean (exit 0).
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → tsgo absent (404);
  fallback `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → clean (exit 0).
- Standalone `npx tsc --noEmit --strict --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters
  --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext` on the new test file → clean
  (root tsconfig `include` covers `src/` only).
- `git fetch origin master` → `origin/master` moved (force update to
  18e41e5038); `git diff HEAD origin/master -- src/core/intent/` is empty —
  the base is still current for this area.
- `git diff --stat` → only `src/core/intent/sweep.ts` modified (+23/−10) and
  the named new test file untracked (376 lines); +389 net lines (< 400).

## Environment note

The worktree's `node_modules/eslint` was missing its `lib/` directory
(partial install). Repaired in place from the `eslint@9.39.5` npm tarball —
no manifest or lockfile changes.

## Preservation evidence

- Deterministic interleave test: `updateIntent` verification evidence and a
  new `addIntent` directive committed while the apply was gated between its
  unlocked read and its write both survive; final record evidence is
  `[note origin, verification concurrent verification, sweep requeue]` and
  the sweep result reports `status:'queued', action:'requeue', updated:1`.
- Child-process test: two concurrent applies plus `addIntent` plus an
  `updateIntent` on an always-fresh record — `updated` multiset is exactly
  `[0,1]` (the second apply computes against the post-sweep locked ledger and
  finds nothing stale), the swept record carries exactly one sweep evidence
  row, and the concurrent directive and edit persist untouched. (The update
  targets a fresh record on purpose: `updateIntent` stamps `lastTouchedAt`
  itself, so an `old`-stamped edit landing between the two serialized sweeps
  would legitimately re-stale and re-sweep the record — order-dependent, not
  a lost write. The deterministic edit-to-the-swept-record case lives in the
  gated in-process test.)
- No-op apply (nothing stale or no ledger) writes nothing and creates no
  ledger; invalid `now` rejects before any store access; a refused write
  (secret-shaped text) leaves persisted bytes untouched and frees the lock
  (retry refuses on text, not contention; manual re-acquire succeeds).

## Remaining limitations

- Two unlocked reads remain on the apply path by design: the no-op pre-check
  (it never drives a write — the locked transaction recomputes, so a
  post-check stale set is authoritative) and the preview path (read-only by
  contract).
- The in-process `Promise.all` and child-barrier tests assert
  order-independent facts; the deterministic forced-interleave coverage lives
  in the gated-read and held-lock tests.
- `src/core/intent/store.ts`'s comment still lists only
  addIntent/updateIntent/importIntentFiles as transacted writers; store.ts
  was out of scope for edits.
</details>

Deep and empty verdicts get `styles.depth + styles.warning`; the single new CSS class is `.depth`, added to the existing shared base-typography rule (no new palette — warning reuses `--status-danger-fg`). - Line ages: the live-queue projection does not expose per-ready-line timestamps, so ready lines are passed as `null` (unknown). Drop files do carry `ageSeconds`, and a stale drop file means dispatchd never ingested it — those real ages feed `lineAgesMs`. No backend route added; existing queries only. ## Files (5, all under src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-queue/) - queue-depth-model.ts (new, ~78 LOC) - queue-depth-model.test.ts (new, ~97 LOC) - FleetQueuePane.depth.test.tsx (new, ~44 LOC) - FleetQueuePane.tsx (+13 LOC) - fleet-queue.module.css (1 line edited) Net LOC: ~+233. ## Commands run - `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-queue/queue-depth-model.test.ts` → 10/10 pass (first run showed the spec's "2-3x" wording expected in text; fixed band label vs the 1–3x ok-window constants, then green). - `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-queue/FleetQueuePane.depth.test.tsx` → 2/2 pass (deep-queue line with warning class; "live capacity unknown." without warning class when fleetSupplyQuery rejects). - `npx eslint` on the four changed TS/TSX files → clean, 0 findings. title: bridge: RQ-PHX-INTENTCONCURRENTWRITERS10SRW1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-INTENTCONCURRENTWRITERS10SRW1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `0ef01dc0e`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-PHX-INTENTCONCURRENTWRITERS10SRW1

## Summary

Preserves PR #4235 intent CRUD/import functionality under simultaneous agent
writes (Mason t1626u shared fleet batching; Nov 5 preservation order). The
ledger store already renamed writes atomically, but `addIntent`,
`updateIntent` and `importIntentFiles` each did an unguarded
`readLedger` → mutate → `writeLedger`, so a concurrent successful write could
be silently overwritten.

All three entry points now run their entire read-modify-write inside a new
`transactIntentLedger` helper in `src/core/intent/store.ts`:

- Per-ledger file lock at `<runs>/intent/ledger.lock` via the existing
  `acquireLocalStoreLockWithOutcome` / `releaseLocalStoreLock` primitive
  (`src/core/fleet/local-store-lock.ts`, same one `authority/ledger.ts`
  uses). Bounded wait (`LOCK_WAIT_MS = 2_000`); contention or an unavailable
  lock throws `IntentError` and never mutates the ledger. The lock is always
  released in `finally`, including refused writes.
- An in-process promise queue per ledger path serializes same-process callers
  so they queue instead of burning the contention budget against themselves.
- Lock anchor is the intent directory itself (`anchorPath: dir`), which
  `directory()` has already verified as an owned, non-symlink, mode-0700
  directory — works for `~/.ashlr-runs` and arbitrary `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` roots.
- Exported signatures and the `ashlr.intent-ledger/v1` schema are unchanged;
  directory/file modes (0700/0600), secret-text refusal, capacity checks,
  provenance and dedupe semantics are preserved.

`importIntentFiles` now parses every input file into `IntentItem`s *before*
acquiring the lock (parsing is side-effect free), then merges inside the
transaction against the freshest ledger — so merge always sees the latest
state and a bad file never contends with or mutates the ledger.

## Changed files (only these)

- `src/core/intent/store.ts` — added `transactIntentLedger` (+ private
  `transactIntentLedgerLocked`, `LOCK_FILE`, `LOCK_WAIT_MS`, `ledgerQueues`).
- `src/core/intent/edit.ts` — `addIntent`/`updateIntent` route through the
  transaction; input validation still happens before the lock.
- `src/core/intent/import.ts` — `importIntentFiles` parses first, merges
  inside the transaction.
- `test/intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1.test.ts` — new suite (6 tests).
- `BRIDGE_NOTES.md` — this file.

`git diff --stat` (working tree vs HEAD): 3 files changed, 110 insertions,
44 deletions, plus the new test (~290 lines) and this file. Net ~+360 LOC,
within the ~400-line budget.

## Test coverage (new file)

- Cross-process: 7 real `tsx` child processes (barrier-synchronized via
  ready/go files, no timing-only assertions) run real `addIntent` /
  `importIntentFiles` / `updateIntent` callers against one scratch root.
  - 5 unique adds + 2 identical adds → all 5 unique survive, the pair merges
    (dedupe), 6 items total.
  - 2 distinct JSONL imports + 1 duplicate import of the same file + 1
    unrelated `updateIntent` → every unique directive present exactly once,
    seeded item updated to `merged`, total 5 items.
- Same-process: 6 parallel `addIntent` calls all survive via the queue.
- Refused write: secret-shaped title (`ghp_…`) and missing-id update both
  throw inside the transaction; ledger bytes identical afterwards and
  `ledger.lock` is gone (release proven); subsequent write succeeds.
- Held lock: `acquireLocalStoreLockWithOutcome` held externally →
  `addIntent` rejects with busy/unavailable after the bounded wait, ledger
  bytes unchanged; after release, writes succeed.
- Independent roots: lock held on root A does not block a write to root B.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1.test.ts`
  → 6/6 pass (~6–13s).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/intent-*.test.ts test/fleet-intent*.test.ts test/m419.remote-handoff-intent.test.ts`
  → 131/132 pass; 1 failure in
  `test/fleet-intent-unified-lifecycle-09sqk1.test.ts` — **pre-existing on
  clean origin/master** (verified via `git stash` + rerun: fails identically
  without this change; the legacy `link`/`ship` CLI replay path appends
  duplicate evidence rows because `pushEvidence` in `evidence.ts` has no
  dedupe — unrelated to this job's scope).
- `npx eslint src/core/intent/{store,edit,import}.ts test/intent-concurrent-writers-10srw1.test.ts`
  → clean (after `npm run install:worktree` healed a partial eslint install).
- `node scripts/check-realio-lane-membership.mjs` → ok, no unclassified
  real-io markers.
- `npx --no-install tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → exit 0 (final
  foreground verification).

## Limitations / remaining legacy writers (explicit, not universal safety)

The transaction covers **only** `addIntent`, `updateIntent` and
`importIntentFiles`. These ledger writers still do unlocked
read-modify-write and can lose each other's (or a transaction's) writes —
documented here rather than claimed safe; they are outside this job's
allowed files:

- `src/core/intent/release.ts` (`noteShippedRelease`)
- `src/core/intent/merge-snapshot.ts` (`noteMergeSnapshot`)
- `src/cli/fleet-intent.ts` `link` verb (readLedger → linkMergedPull →
  writeLedger)
- `src/cli/fleet-intent-evidence.ts` merged dry-run/apply path
- Direct `writeLedger` callers anywhere else (exported, still lock-free by
  design for seed/test use)

Other notes:

- `mutate` callbacks must not re-enter `transactIntentLedger` for the same
  ledger (would self-deadlock the in-process queue); documented on the
  export.
- Lock wait is a fixed 2 s bound; under heavier contention writers fail
  with "Intent ledger is busy" rather than queueing — deliberate per spec
  (bounded, no indefinite waits, no silent retries of side effects).
- The new test file uses real child processes but stays in the unit lane:
  children are short barrier-synchronized tsx evals, and the real-io lane
  membership list (`test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs`) is outside this
  job's allowed paths. If CI load ever makes it flaky, move it to
  `REAL_IO_TEST_FILES` in a follow-up.
- `origin/master` advanced one unrelated commit (60635cad, #4728, web-ui
  only) during this work; no overlap with `src/core/intent`. Changes left
  uncommitted as instructed.
</details>

# Leader reply relay restart preservation

Original: [phantom #4370](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/pull/4370), head `ce3c979f7e077fbc4039faa4bc69fdb4eba3bc98`. Compared against checked-out, freshly fetched master `826e611ede8c14477e756418c3d2db5ee28aa966`, using only the four requested provenance files. Final fetch moved `origin/master` to `10728d5009acfa447546ac734f452de3243d9235`; the evidence below is for the checked-out SHA, not that newer commit.

| Behavior | Original/current comparison and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| CLI sync and receipt persistence | Both contain the sync command and persisted pending/posted receipts. New subprocess test invokes the actual CLI twice with isolated HOME and runs directory: two distinct replies are posted once, then both receipts are skipped. |
| Thread and source | Both append answers to the thread with Telegram pending. The test checks exact synthetic reply text, pending delivery without `sentAt`, and unchanged PLAN-LOG bytes. No transport is invoked. |
| Interrupted receipt | Both retain a pending receipt as uncertain and skip it. The test changes a persisted receipt to pending between CLI processes, observes exit 1 and `unknown`, and verifies the thread bytes do not change. This models the persisted crash state, not an actual crash or a delivery receipt. |
| Parsing difference | Current master deduplicates identical text on the same date and retains the last reply under a dated heading; original did not. The original test expected two identical same-day replies, while current expects one. The new evidence uses distinct headings and texts and does not claim exact preservation of that original duplicate behavior. |

Residual gaps: original identical same-day reply behavior differs as described; a separate owner must decide whether it should be restored. End-to-end Telegram/iMessage delivery, actual crash timing, concurrent syncs, and the later master SHA were not tested. No production files were changed. This evidence alone does not authorize closing the original.

1. **Lint (authority 3/3), real errors.**
   - `.github/scripts/ci-mcp-selection.mjs`: no Node globals. Added the
     `/* global process, console */` pragma its siblings use.
   - `scripts/measure-desktop-perf.mjs`: `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout`/`WebSocket`
     undeclared. Added a pragma.
   - `test/setup/child-process-home.cjs`: `.cjs` matched no config block.
     Added a one-file block in `eslint.config.js` (test/setup is owner-reviewed).
   - `idea-steer-model.ts` and its test: intentional control-char regexes.
     Added `eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex` with a reason, matching
     the existing convention.
   - `lint:realio-lane`: four suites that really spawn children were missing from
     `REAL_IO_TEST_FILES`: constitution-recutnonphxold60, phantom-discovery,
     release-articles and fleet-coordination.
2. **`check:release` (authority 1/3), stale contracts.**
   - `cli-registry-drift`: `wb` and `constitution` were dispatched but missing from
     `TOP_LEVEL_COMMANDS`. `wb` had no `HELP_ENTRIES` row, so one was added.
   - `documentation-navigation`: `docs/README.md` linked the source-only guides
     PHANTOM-DISCOVERY.md and FABLE-ORCHESTRATOR.md relatively, which breaks in
     the npm package. They now use absolute GitHub URLs, like fleet-health.md.
   - `m30.ci.test.ts`: it still asserted the values from before #4600 and #4592:
     `tsc` typecheck scripts and the old concurrency group. Both changes were
     deliberate. #4600 moved the no-emit gate to tsgo, with parity proven by
     `scripts/tsgo-parity.mjs`, and emission stays on tsc. #4592 gave
     release-gate dispatches a per-tag group. The assertions now match, with
     comments explaining why.
   - `m33.release-meta`: #4677 added `release-isolated-tree.test.mjs` to
     `check:pack-contracts` without updating the pinned list.

     README table.
   - `docs-sync`: regenerated docs/cli.md, CLI-REFERENCE.md, QUICKSTART.md,
     examples/quickstart.md and site/llms-full.txt.
   - `m420.remote-handoff-recovery` was not hermetic. `remote-handoff.ts` calls
     `gh` through `credentialExecFileSync`, which first probes the real PATH for a
     Secrets binary. An unreadable PATH entry (EACCES/EPERM, as with
     Windows `WindowsApps`) or an installed Secrets CLI changed the result. This
     is most likely the Windows "portability overflow" failure. The test now
     routes the wrapper to its existing `execFileSync` double.
   - `release-articles` caught a real product bug. `release-public-facts.ts` pins
     the exact SHA-256 of `ci.yml`. #4592 changed `ci.yml` after the last re-pin
     (#4454), so release verification refused the current workflow, including the
     source of the published v3.30.31 (`c2a41bf9...`). Pinned `c2a41bf9...` (the
     v3.30.31 source) and `a0aaa485...` (current master). The prior pins stay.
     The topology checks are unchanged, and only exact reviewed bytes are added.

## Not resolved

- **Mac exhaustive "Build" exit 134**, at about 110 s into the step. I could not
  get the job logs (no gh auth in this sandbox). It is not a tsc heap OOM:
  `tsc -p tsconfig.json` with emit passes under `--max-old-space-size=2048`
  (peak RSS 2.3 GB). I made no workflow change. It needs the job log to diagnose.
- Some failures are local to this machine and do not appear in CI evidence:
  companion-inventory, universe-portfolio-delivery-integration, m286 timeouts,
  npm-cli-launch, and sandbox-exec suites. The cause is Homebrew Node 26 with a
  missing `lib/node_modules`, a sandbox-denied `~/.local/bin`, and nested
  sandbox-exec. The affected source and tests are unchanged since Nov 6, and the
  Nov 9 scheduled run was green.

## Commands run (temp HOME, `~/.local/bin` dropped from PATH)

- `npm run lint`: PASS, 0 errors and 267 warnings, which are pre-existing.
  Both lane lints pass.
- `npm run typecheck:fast`: PASS
- `npm run check:docs`: PASS, 0 errors
- `npm run check:release`: PASS, 289 passed and 1 skipped (it was 10 failed before)
- `npm run test:ci` on the touched and drift suites (m420, readme-command-table,
  docs-sync, doc-facts, the realio additions, release-articles,
  typecheck-fast-projects, authority-codeowners, authority-tier1-closure, m30,
  cli-registry-drift, documentation-navigation): 13 files, 390 passed
- `npm run test:ci -- test/m33.release-meta.test.ts test/fleet-coordination.test.ts`:
  52 passed
- `vitest --config vite.config.web.ts idea-steer-model.test.ts`: 5 passed
- `node --test .github/tests/ci-mcp-selection.test.mjs`: 2 passed. With
  ci-mac-rotation it was 5 passed.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`, run once: PASS on every stage
- A full local `test:ci --shard=2/3` hit the 30-minute local hard cap. Its
  failures were triaged file by file as described above.

## Net LOC

19 files: +61 / -13, net +48. Excludes this file.

body:

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** .github/scripts/ci-pack-smoke.mjs .github/scripts/release-fast-smoke.mjs .github/tests/ci-pack-smoke.test.mjs .github/tests/ci-release-same-runner.test.mjs .github/tests/release-isolated-tree.test.mjs .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml scripts/build-outputs.mjs scripts/release-isolated-tree.mjs scripts/release-smoke-timing.mjs test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-RELEASE-ISOLATED-BUILD-1

Make "source changed after build" structurally impossible. Follow-up to #4562.
All changes are uncommitted in this worktree. Nothing was committed, pushed,
tagged or published, and no PR comment was posted.

## Root cause (verified)

`npm run build` ran `node scripts/generate-docs-llms.mjs`, which **rewrites the
tracked `docs/llms.txt`** whenever a docs page lands without regenerating it.
Master is stale right now: FABLE-ORCHESTRATOR.md and PHANTOM-DISCOVERY.md are
missing from it. So every release build dirtied the tree, and step 11 refused
with "source changed after build" (runs 42728489451 and 42737802873). In a
clean clone of master, `npm ci && build-sea && prepare-sidecar && tauri build`
left exactly one tracked change: ` M docs/llms.txt`.

## Changes

1. **Isolated pinned tree** (`scripts/release-isolated-tree.mjs`, new).
   - `create <path>` runs `git worktree add --detach <path> <sha>` with the SHA
     from ASHLR_RELEASE_SHA or GITHUB_SHA. The path must be absent or an empty
     `mktemp -d` directory. Hooks are disabled, and the new tree must be pristine.
   - `verify <root>` is strict. It refuses a moved HEAD and
     `git diff --exit-code <sha>` changes in the worktree and in the index
     (bytes, modes, deletions, additions). It also refuses untracked unignored
     files, hidden `assume-unchanged`/`skip-worktree` flags (git status cannot
     see those), and any ignored file outside the declared build-output
     inventory. That last check catches a new `.gitignore` or an edited
     `info/exclude` that hides a write.
   - In `ci.yml`, `release-build` creates `$RUNNER_TEMP/phantom-release-tree`
     right after Node setup. The build, custody capture and smoke steps run there
     (`working-directory`), never in the job checkout. The build step runs
     `verify` after the nightly build and again after `prepare` (pack).
   - The tree path is fixed, not random, so the native cache path stays stable
     across runs. Creation still refuses an existing non-empty path.
2. **ci-pack-smoke** `source()` now uses the same `sourceDrift` check, replacing
   the `git status`-only check. The refusal test from #4562 is kept. Added tests
   for an injected tracked-file edit during pack (`M .gitignore`) and for a
   skip-worktree-hidden edit.
3. **Generated outputs.**
   - The build no longer runs `generate-docs-llms.mjs`; staleness is the docs
     test's job (`test/docs-agent-parity.test.ts`). `docs/llms.txt` is
     regenerated and committed; the generator is deterministic.
   - `scripts/build-outputs.mjs` lists every in-tree path that each
     `npm run build` command and each desktop nightly step writes.
   - `test/build-outputs.test.ts` checks that the inventory equals the real
     `package.json` build segments and `buildStepPlan()`. It also checks that
     every release output is gitignored by committed rules and untracked, and
     that icon regeneration (tracked rasters) is never in the release lane.
   - All 32,365 ignored files the real clean-clone build left matched the
     inventory, with 0 undeclared.
4. **Runtime.**
   - The cargo cache key is `Cargo.lock` only (`release-native-v2-…`), with
     no `github.sha`. Before, the key changed on every commit, so every green
     run saved a new entry (median 25.5 s post-save, 4/4 runs), and 8/10 restores
     were 0–1 s, meaning nothing usable was restored.
   - The pinned npm/Tauri CLI install runs in the background while Bun, Rust
     and the cache restore. A gate step checks its exit status, with a 5-minute
     timeout.
   - Smoke runs the native launch (now async) and the updater feed read
     concurrently.
   - Fail-fast step timeouts: build 45 min, smoke 6 min (the phase deadline is
     5 min plus 5 s).
   - `release-desktop.yml` dropped its duplicate `npm run build` (build-sea.mjs
     already builds).
   - Attestation already reuses the uploaded artifact and never rebuilds; the
     build-once-reuse path ("Find existing immutable build") is unchanged.
   - Attest, sign, notarize, secret gates and the SHA-pinned secret gate are
     untouched. No permissions, `secrets.*`, triggers or third-party actions
     were added.
5. **Tag-vs-master custody** (CI Efficiency item 3) had already landed in #4577:
   `producerRef` and the job's `if` both admit the ancestor stable tag. Its 3/10
   baseline failures (v3.30.28, step 12) predate that merge. No further change.
6. **Measurement.** `docs/release/SMOKE-TIMING.md` holds the real last-10 baseline,
   read from the public Actions API (`gh` could not read its config in this
   sandbox). `scripts/release-smoke-timing.mjs` provides `list` and `append`; the
   append is deterministic and idempotent and tracks the next 5 smokes. Tests are
   in `test/release-smoke-timing.test.ts`.

## Before / after

- **Before (measured):** pass **4/10**, median **396.5 s**, p95 **462.9 s**.
  The median and p95 match CI Efficiency exactly; they reported 5/10, but the
  job records show 4 green. All 10 runs built from source. The build step median
  is 315 s. Reuse runs took 48–95 s.
- **After: not measured yet.** It needs merged runs; `append` records them.
  Expected:
  - 2/10 drift failures removed (the root cause).
  - 3/10 custody failures already fixed by #4577.
  - About 25 s post-cache save gone on an exact hit, plus warm cargo deps.
  - About 5 s from the tool-install overlap.
  - More green builds means more 48–95 s reuse runs.

  These are estimates, not measurements.

PR comment for CI Efficiency (not posted):
> Desktop release smoke before: pass 4/10, median 396.5 s, p95 462.9 s
> (runs 42335580261..42737802873). Two failures were build-time drift from
> `generate-docs-llms.mjs` rewriting tracked `docs/llms.txt`; that is now removed
> from the build, and builds run in a detached pinned worktree with a strict
> verify. Three failures were tag custody, already fixed by #4577. The cargo cache
> is now keyed by lockfile only (it saved about 25 s on every run before). After
> numbers will be appended by `node scripts/release-smoke-timing.mjs append` over
> the next 5 release smokes.

## Commands run and results

The worktree's own `node_modules` is incomplete (ESLint `lib/cli` is missing),
so lint, `verify-changed` and the pack contracts ran in a clean `git clone` of
this HEAD with my changes copied in (`/tmp/rq-iso-EPPY/tree`, fresh `npm ci`).

- `node --test .github/tests/release-isolated-tree.test.mjs`: **16/16 pass**.
- `node --test .github/tests/ci-release-same-runner.test.mjs`: **4/4 pass**.
- `npm run check:pack-contracts`, with my changes against pristine master in
  the same clone:
  - Mine: 726 tests, 705 pass, 21 fail. Master: 705 tests, 685 pass, 20 fail.
  - The only new name is the upload-watchdog CPU-timing test, in a file I did
    not touch. It passes 3/3 run alone (load flake).
  - All other failures also fail on master, from host policy: setuid `chmod`
    is EPERM, and signed SEA / `.app` creation is EPERM.
- ci-pack-smoke + isolated tree + same-runner + fast-smoke + local-input:
  **221 pass, 1 fail**. The failure is the setuid "special file bits" test,
  which needs `chmod 4644`, and this host refuses it.
- vitest (`build-outputs`, `release-smoke-timing`, `m30.ci`, `doc-facts`,
  `docs-agent-parity`, `m468`, `desktop-nightly-build`): **96/97 pass**. The
  failure is desktop-nightly's `.app` packaging, the same host EPERM as the
  real Tauri bundle step; the script is unchanged.
- ESLint on all touched code files: clean. In `verify-changed.mjs`:
  - `tsgo --noEmit`: PASS. Web typecheck: PASS.
  - The ESLint and realio failures it reported come from files outside this
    change (its base in the clone was wider).
  - My `test/build-outputs.test.ts` realio violation is fixed (it is now in the
    real-io lane).
- `npm run check:docs`: 0 errors. `generate-docs-llms.mjs --check`: lists all
  384 pages.
- A real `npm run build` in this worktree wrote no tracked or unignored file
  and left 0 undeclared outputs. The command exited 1 at the dependency
  inventory's `npm pack` because of the broken local `node_modules`; the same
  step passed in the clean clone.

## Net LOC

+947 / −27 (net +920) across 17 files. That includes about 450 lines of tests
and 94 lines of the timing doc.

## Not done / follow-ups

- No live CI run of the new workflow; the first scheduled release smoke after
  merge is the proof. `rustup` and the native toolchain are unchanged, since
  `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is kept.
- Consider adding `generate-docs-llms.mjs --check` to the Quick typecheck gate so
  stale indexes fail at PR time. I left it out because merge-queue conflicts
  between concurrent docs PRs could cause churn.
- `selectRun('build')` only reuses builds from master-branch runs, not from
  earlier tag-dispatch runs on the same SHA. That is a missed reuse, not a
  failure, and it is security-sensitive, so I left it.
</details>

(`GET /api/verse/fleet/runs`) reads a **healthy** merge window with items, it now

intent ledger: each pull is linked to directives by `linkMergedPull` (RQ keys in
title/branch), records a `pr` evidence row and a merged `prs` association, and
advances status only for `queued`/`in-progress` items. Evidence already recorded
short-circuits the link, so repeat snapshots never rewrite an unchanged ledger.

(`docs/intent-preservation-4235.md`) lists as missing from retained PR #4235.

## Summary

#3154 (RQ-APPTRUTH-6-SOURCEOFTRUTHR2) is the oldest open PR in 3000-3999 that touches the
desktop console and still has work missing from master. #4229 (RQ-APPTRUTH-6-SPLIT) already landed
its forum core (`src/core/fleet/forum/{canon,keys,policy,store,types}.ts`, byte-identical). Its
service, the verse route and the desktop Forum pane were never landed.

This recut lands the desktop read slice:

- `src/core/fleet/forum/view.ts` (new): `forumRoot()`, `projectForum()`, `readForum()`. This is the
  read-only projection from #3154's `service.ts`, rebuilt on master's existing `readState`. It never
  takes the lock and never writes. A forum that was never written projects as the five default
  channels. Per-channel and per-thread counts take one pass, where #3154 ran an O(channels×posts)
  filter.
- `src/core/verse/forum-api.ts` (new): `GET /api/verse/forum[?channel=&thread=&limit=]`. It needs a
  current read session (401). Writes get 405. Unknown or repeated query keys, an unknown channel and
  a limit outside 1-100 get 400 `{v:1,ok:false,reason:'invalid'}`. An unreadable store or a relative
  `ASHLR_FORUM_ROOT` gets 503 `unavailable`, never a guessed empty board. The storage root is never a
  query parameter.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-forum/**` (taken by path from pr-3154): the Forum pane, ForumBoard,
  the strict `narrowForum` shape guard, the query, CSS and the 4 PR unit tests. Changes from the PR:
  the empty-board text and the 405 message no longer point at `phm forum` / `phantom_forum`, because
  neither exists on master.

Left out (separate concerns, too large for a ~400-line recut): the forum write service (post, wakes,
commitments sweep, standup), the `phm forum` CLI, the `phantom_forum` MCP tool, channel ingest, the
mobile ForumScreen and the Mission SSE stream.

## OWNER STEP REQUIRED: mount the route

The route is **not mounted**, so until it is, the pane shows "Forum is not in this build." (the
narrowed 404 path). Mounting it in `DEFAULT_API_MODULES` (`src/core/verse/verse-api.ts`) pulls
`forum-api.ts`, `forum/view.ts`, `forum/store.ts` and `forum/types.ts` into the Tier-1 authority
import closure. `test/authority-tier1-closure-310b.test.ts` then fails ("closure has not grown"), and
`test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts` pins the exact mount list. Both of these files and
`test/fixtures/authority/**` are in CODEOWNERS, and this job may not touch them. I tried the mount,
saw the gate fail, and reverted it. I did not evade the gate with a non-literal import. To mount it
(owner):

1. In `src/core/verse/verse-api.ts`, add `| 'forum'` to `MountedApiModuleId` and append this entry to

## Known gap: argv dispatch is dormant by design

On master, `phm fleet <verb>` dispatches only through the generated
`FLEET_SUBCOMMAND_LOADERS` (`src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`), which the
task forbids editing (4-path cap; `gen-fleet-registry.mjs --check` also runs in
`verify-changed.mjs` and `fleet-subcommand-registry.test.ts`). The module
therefore exports `cmdFleetRetryEmpty` as a **non-async** `export function`
returning `Promise<number>` — the same contract the loader calls — which the
generator intentionally skips (it only registers `export async function` /
`export const X = async (`), matching the `src/cli/fleet-nodes.ts` precedent.
The preservation test drives the real resolution path
(`resolveFleetSubcommand('retry-empty')` → module import →
`loaded[exportName](rest)`), proving convention compliance.
