export to `export async function` and run
`node scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`. That is a 2-line diff outside this
task's allowed paths. Because this routing gap exists, this notes file does
**not** ask for `Closes #4501`; the bridge may decide whether activating the
verb now (regenerating the registry) or landing the dormant module is right.

## Receipt-before-queue crash semantics (verbatim from original)

Apply takes `ready.lock`, re-reads the queue, refuses if the snapshot changed,
then writes receipt files **before** replacing the queue. A crash between a
receipt fsync and the queue rename leaves a receipt without a queued line: the
job can never be retried again (receipt persists) and needs manual recovery —
there is **no transaction guaranteeing enqueue**; ordering only guarantees
never-enqueue-twice. Conversely a crash before any receipt leaves nothing
recorded and a later run retries normally. Unrelated queue bytes, other READY
lines and prior receipts are preserved (snapshot verified, append-only output,
atomic rename).

# FIXUP-CI-phantom-auto-tag-829874

## Summary

Auto-tag failed on master at a8c04fe4a5 (run 42753829874) in the step
"Mint ashlr-release App token". #4607 added `permission-actions: write` to the
ashlr-release App mints in auto-tag.yml and release-train.yml. The App
installation does not grant `actions`, so `actions/create-github-app-token`
got a 422 ("The permissions requested are not granted to this installation").

Root cause: a real workflow bug, not a flaky test. It is already fixed on
master by #4608 (751ef03a1f). That change dropped the actions request from both
mints and dispatched CI with the job GITHUB_TOKEN instead. No workflow edit is
needed here, so none was made.

What this change adds: a guard against the same mistake happening again. Before
this, only Auto-tag's mint was asserted, but #4607 broke the release-train mint
too. The new test in `.github/tests/release-train.test.mjs`
("every ashlr-release App mint requests only permissions the installation
grants") scans every workflow for each `create-github-app-token` step that uses
`ASHLR_RELEASE_APP_ID`. It requires that each one:
- requests at least one `permission-*` (an unscoped mint inherits every grant);
- requests only `permission-contents` or `permission-pull-requests`.

It also requires mints to exist in auto-tag.yml, release-please.yml and
release-train.yml, so the scan cannot pass by matching nothing.

The granted set is assumed to be contents and pull-requests, the permissions
that minted successfully before #4607. Any future widening of the list must
come with the matching App installation grant.

suppression in the recut loop and in the shared launch precheck. Protected
worker prompts (`precheck.sh`, staging copies) untouched.

## What changed

- `src/core/fleet/recut-loop.ts` — new `empty-yield` guard: when the last
  `EMPTY_YIELD_STREAK` (2) ledger attempts this loop wrote for one PR on the
  *same head SHA* all finished empty in `jobs.jsonl`, the candidate is
  skipped (`{pr, reason: 'empty-yield'}` in the tick's `skipped` report —
  the avoided-launch record) and no drop file or ledger line is minted. A
  moved head is different work and recovers; missing ledger entries,
  unmeasured/productive/merged outcomes, or outcome rows older than
  `EMPTY_YIELD_WINDOW_MS` (7 days) each fail open. Outcome evidence shares
  the same bounded `jobs.jsonl` tail read the in-flight scan already
  performs (`readInflightPrs` now returns `{prs, metricsText}`).
- `contrib/mac/launch_precheck.py` — `precheck()` returns `(14,
  "empty_streak_<N>x")` before spawning `precheck.sh` when the job id has
  >= `EMPTY_STREAK` (2) consecutive trailing empty finishes in
  `metrics/jobs.jsonl` (bounded 8 MiB tail, size/mtime-cached, malformed
  rows ignored). dispatchd logs `DONE-NOOP <job> [precheck code=14
  empty_streak_Nx]`, appends `queue/precheck-skips.tsv` and emits
  `precheck_skip`; restock records the job done. Unmeasured finishes,

  ledgers all fail open — suppression is advisory.

Base: origin/master `02b28e092891d6cda9f05788871979f84af9bd26` after `git fetch origin master` and fast-forward. No production code was changed: the proof passed on master. This is a synthetic code-path proof, not evidence that either historical Slack message received a reply in production.

## Path traced

- `src/cli/channels-slack.ts` wires `openSlackSocket` to `createSlackLeaderAdapter` with `ownerStatusReply()`.
- `src/core/agents/slack-transport.ts` `openSlackSocket` receives the socket delivery, calls `unwrapSlackSocketEnvelope` and the adapter's `normalize` and `route` functions.
- `src/core/agents/slack-inbound.ts` `slackEventToBus` checks team, channel, sender and event, and maps the root message timestamp into the Slack channel/thread reference.
- `src/core/agents/slack-leader.ts` `ingestSlackLeaderEnvelope` verifies the configured owner and authenticated human identity, calls `createLeaderNetwork().ingest`, then checks `statusReply.ask` and calls `compose` and `network.reply`.
- `src/core/agents/owner-status-reply.ts` `isOwnerStatusRequest` recognizes the exact request; `composeOwnerStatusReply` calls `leaderDailyBrief` in `src/core/comms/leader-daily-brief.ts`, which reads recorded shipped, needs, quota and proposal status. This path does not use `fleet-status-cache.ts`.
- `src/core/agents/leader-network.ts` `reply` records and routes the reply; `deliverSlackLeaderMessage` in `slack-leader.ts` calls `deliverSlackEnvelope`. `slackOutboundPlan` in `src/core/agents/slack-audience.ts` extracts the thread root; `deliverSlackEnvelope` posts `thread_ts` in `slack-transport.ts` and the network records `reply.delivered` after success.

The inbox is append-only, so the test checks the corresponding durable `reply.delivered` marker, which excludes the request from `pending()`, rather than expecting the inbox text to be rewritten.
